discovery.about: obscura-cli, the obscura and obscura-worker binaries: fetch, serve, scrape and mcp subcommands, global flags and the scrape worker protocol.
discovery.see: The obscura command: clap definitions for global flags (proxy, stealth, robots, user agent, storage dir, private network, V8 flags) and the fetch, serve, scrape and mcp subcommands; fetch dumps, eval and screenshots with adaptive settle, serve workers and ready files, scrape fan-out to workers, and a process hard deadline.

The obscura-worker helper used by scrape: reads newline-delimited JSON commands (navigate, evaluate, title, dump_html, dump_text and others) from stdin and writes one JSON response per command, including the final navigation HTTP status.
Build script that appends the git commit to the workspace version for local builds so different checkouts can be told apart, while tarball and minimal-image builds keep the bare version.
End-to-end MCP client tests against obscura mcp using a loopback fixture instead of public sites: protocol initialization, navigation, snapshots and evaluation through the tool interface.

Tests that fetch --screenshot captures after --eval scrolls the live page, uses live animation time unless a harness pins a sample, and that paired captures reassert scroll and read state after the final settle.
Tests for serve --ready-file: ephemeral-port servers publish distinct usable ports, an unwritable ready path fails startup, and a ready file is rejected with multiple workers.

Tests for obscura serve with multiple workers: worker processes that are killed are reaped and replaced by fresh workers, and the CDP discovery endpoint keeps answering correctly instead of being poisoned.

Tests the worker navigation status field: the main document's final HTTP code after redirects, null for blocked or non-HTTP navigations, and error envelopes for failures, using offline blocklist cases.
Tests that CLI and stdio MCP private-network denials explain the --allow-private-network opt-in without granting access, and that cloud metadata denials never suggest relaxing the guard.

Tests that --obey-robots propagates from the CLI into a scrape worker: a disallowed fetch fails, and the local test server sees only the robots.txt request, checking policy propagation rather than startup speed.

Screenshot regression test checking pixel colors that an outset box-shadow is painted outside an element whose border box is transparent, while the area inside the border box stays unpainted, as in Chromium.
Regression test that fetch --dump text preserves the whitespace between adjacent inline spans, so words in separate inline elements are not glued together in the extracted text.
